overview: S00 is the server's keep-alive probe: the client must echo the id back in C00. Anticheats use the round trip as their latency clock: the server records when it sent each id and when the matching reply arrives, which yields the player's ping and exposes ping-spoof, timer and connection-manipulation cheats. The corpus shows the same echo-tracking pattern at every scale, from the four-line ConnectionManager in Frequency to NCP's keepalive-frequency check with kick actions and Grim's validation that the replied id was actually sent.

checks.name: BadPacketsO (Grim)
checks.purpose: Flags keep-alive replies whose id was never sent by the server, the signature of a spoofed or replayed keep-alive stream.
checks.how_it_works: Tracks every OUT keep-alive id in a queue. On the IN keep-alive reply, searches the queue for the id: a match removes the id (pruning the queue) and passes, while a reply with an unknown id flags and cancels the packet.
checks.detects: Ping-spoof clients that fabricate keep-alive replies, and lag-switch or timer tools that replay stale ids.
checks.variations: Hydro's KeepAliveTracker and Frequency's ConnectionManager implement the same echo matching; only Grim validates and cancels the reply.

checks.name: KeepAliveAdapter + KeepAliveFrequency (NoCheatPlus)
checks.purpose: Limits keep-alive reply frequency and records last keep-alive timing for the god-mode and moving checks.
checks.how_it_works: ProtocolLib adapter on both keep-alive directions: the receiving side always updates lastKeepAliveTime (even when the check is disabled, because fight.godmode depends on it) and runs the KeepAliveFrequency check, which cancels the reply when the frequency exceeds the configured limits; the sending side records the outgoing id so the expected-reply model stays consistent.
checks.detects: Keep-alive spam, timer manipulation that shows up as impossible reply frequency, and the desync that ping-spoofing produces.
checks.variations: Frequency's ConnectionManager keeps the same last-sent-time map but only computes ping; NCP adds frequency limits and actions.

checks.name: KeepAliveTracker (Hydro)
checks.purpose: Tracks the keep-alive round trip as the player's latency clock, feeding ping data to every other check.
checks.how_it_works: On the OUT keep-alive, stores the id with a send timestamp in an expected map. On the IN reply, looks up the id, removes it and computes keepAlivePing as the receive timestamp minus the send timestamp, setting the acceptedKeepAlive flag. The ping value is displayed in the /hydro debug command and feeds the ping-based exclusions.
checks.detects: Ping spoofing is exposed because the computed ping diverges from the transport-level expectation; the tracker itself is data, not a flagger.
checks.variations: Frequency and Tecnio's ConnectionTracker use the identical map-and-measure pattern; Hydro exposes the value to its GUI and checks.

checks.name: ConnectionManager (Frequency)
checks.purpose: Converts keep-alive and transaction echoes into a measured ping that every check reads for latency exemptions.
checks.how_it_works: TickManager sends the OUT keep-alive and stores the id with a timestamp; the incoming processor calls onKeepAlive when the reply arrives. ConnectionManager looks up the recorded send time for that id and stores the difference as keepAlivePing. PingSpoofA/B and the lag exemptions then compare this keep-alive ping against the transaction ping.
checks.detects: Ping-spoof and timer cheats: a keep-alive ping that disagrees with the transaction ping is the flag condition in PingSpoofA.
checks.variations: Hydro's KeepAliveTracker is the same pattern; Frequency pairs it with the transaction clock, which Hydro handles in a separate tracker.
